title: Study of MDX2003 in Participants with Relapsed/Refractory B-Cell Malignancies
official: A phase 1/2 clinical study evaluating MDX2003 in participants with relapsed, progressive, or refractory B-cell malignancies
summary: Main objective: Evaluate the safety and tolerability of MDX2003 in participants with advanced B-cell malignancies. Part A: Identify the recommended doses for expansion for further development of MDX2003. Part B: Assess the preliminary anti-lymphoma activity of MDX2003.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. [1] Participant provides informed consent to participate in the study prior to undergoing any study procedures.
2. [10] Male participants with female sexual partners of childbearing potential must agree to use highly effective form of contraception while receiving study drug and for 6 months (or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer) after the last dose of any study drug.
3. [11] Participant is willing and able to comply with scheduled study visits and procedures.
4. [12] Participant must have discontinued any other investigational agent at least 4 weeks or 5 half-lives prior to the first dose of study drug, whichever is longer.
5. [13] Participant must have discontinued other anticancer interventions before Cycle 1 Day 1 as follows: (a) Chemoimmunotherapy, toxin-conjugated compounds, or biologic therapy (eg, antibodies) for at least 4 weeks or 5 half-lives for biologic therapy, whichever is shorter; (b) Radio-conjugated compounds for at least 8 weeks; (c) Radiotherapy for at least 4 weeks, except for limited field palliative radiotherapy to nontarget lesion, which may be completed at least 7 days before Cycle 1 Day 1; (d) CAR T-cell therapy for at least 4 weeks.
6. [2] Participant is ≥18 years old.
7. [3] Part A: Participant has one of the following confirmed diagnoses according to WHO 2016 or 2022 criteria, has relapsed or progressed on at least 2 prior lines of therapy: (●) LBCL (including DLBCL, HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements, PMBCL, etc.); (●) FL Grade 1 to 3B; (●) MCL; (●) MZL (splenic, nodal, extranodal); (●) Transformation of indolent B-cell lymphoma and Richter’s Transformation into DLBCL; (●) Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma; (●) WM requires SRC approval prior to enrollment. Part B: Participants with selected B-cell malignancy according to WHO 2016 or 2022 criteria. Prior therapy may include the following: (●) At least 2 therapies, including an anti-CD20 mAb-containing chemotherapy combination regimen. If a CAR T-cell therapy is approved for the disease and available in the participating country, then participants must have relapsed or be ineligible for CAR T-cell therapy. In countries where appropriate, DLBCL participants with 1 prior line of therapy who are CAR T-cell therapy ineligible and do not have other effective treatment options available may be enrolled. (●) Participants with MCL must have either failed BTKi or be intolerant to BTKi. (●) Participants with indolent lymphoma must have need for treatment initiation based on symptoms and/or disease burden. For both Part A and Part B, prior therapy may include the following: Participants must have previously received a CD20×CD3 bispecific antibody, where clinically appropriate and available, or be considered ineligible for such therapy.
8. [4] Participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 0 to 2 (enrollment of participants with ECOG PS 2 requires sponsor discussion).
9. [5] Participant has documented CD19 or CD20 positivity of their B-cell neoplasm based on any representative pathology report from the past 3 months.
10. [6] Participant has measurable disease, defined as at least 1 bi-dimensionally measurable nodal lesion, defined as >1.5 cm in its longest dimension, or at least 1 bi-dimensionally measurable extranodal lesion, defined as >1.0 cm in its longest dimension by computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or positron emission tomography (PET)-CT.
11. [7] Participant has adequate organ function, as defined by the following laboratory values obtained within 14 days prior to the first dose of study drug(s): Hemoglobin ≥9.0 g/dL (≥5.6 mmol/L) without PRBC transfusion within 7 days; Absolute neutrophil count ≥1,000/mm^3 (1 x 10^9/L) without growth-factor support for at least 7 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 for short-acting G-CSF products and at least 14 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 for long-acting G-CSF products (G-CSF permitted for participants with initial bone marrow involvement); Platelet count ≥50,000/mm^3 (50 x 10^9/L) without platelet transfusion within 7 days; Total serum bilirubin ≤1.5 x ULN (≤3 x ULN if attributable to known Gilbert’s syndrome or documented liver involvement with lymphoma); AST ≤3 x ULN (≤5 × ULN in participants with documented liver involvement by lymphoma) (based on institutional limits); ALT ≤3 x ULN (≤5 × ULN in participants with documented liver involvement by lymphoma) (based on institutional limits); Estimated creatinine clearance or creatinine Serum creatinine of ≤1.5 x ULN (based on institutional limits) OR a measured creatinine clearance of >50 mL/min OR a calculated creatinine clearance of ≥50 mL/min by the CKD-EPI equation. (Abbreviations: ALT=alanine aminotransferase; AST=aspartate aminotransferase; CKD-EPI=chronic kidney disease epidemiology collaboration; G-CSF=granulocyte colony-stimulating factor; PRBC=packed red blood cell; ULN=upper limit of normal)
12. [8] Female participants of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to the first dose of study drug(s).
13. [9] Female participants of childbearing potential must agree to follow instructions for highly effective method(s) of contraception while receiving study drug and for 6 months (or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer) after the last dose of study drug.
Exclusion criteria:
1. [2] Participant has known or suspected history of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
2. [3] Participant has unresolved toxicity from previous anticancer therapy (other than CTCAE Grade ≤2 alopecia or neuropathy) that contraindicates participation in the study in the opinion of the investigator.
3. [4] Participant has primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma or known CNS involvement with lymphoma at screening.
4. [5] Participant has any of the following conditions related to cardiac function: (a) Congestive heart failure (New York Heart Association Class III to IV) and/or known decreased ejection fraction of <45%; (b) Myocardial infarction or transient ischemic attacks within 6 months prior to Cycle 1 Day 1; (c) Onset of unstable angina pectoris within 6 months prior to Cycle 1 Day 1; (d) Any other clinically significant cardiac abnormality.
5. [6] Participant has known past or current malignancy other than inclusion diagnosis, except for the following: (a) Cervical carcinoma of Stage 1B or less; (b) Non-invasive basal cell or squamous cell skin carcinoma; (c) Non-invasive, superficial bladder cancer; (d) Prostate cancer with a current prostate-specific antigen level <0.1 ng/mL; (e) Any curable cancer with a CR of >2 years duration.
6. [7] Participant has a history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that may prevent, limit, or confound the protocol-specified assessments; interfere with the participant’s participation for the full duration of the study; or indicate a condition for which study participation is not in the best interest (eg, compromises the well-being) of the participant, in the opinion of the investigator.
7. [8] Participant has an active, uncontrolled infection that is Grade ≥3 according to CTCAE V5.0, or an infection requiring systemic anti-infective therapy that remains clinically unstable in the opinion of the investigator.
8. [9] Participant has confirmed history of autoimmune disease (or other diseases) requiring chronic systemic steroid (>10 mg/day systemic prednisone or equivalent of >140 mg over the last 14 days prior to first dose of MDX2003) or immunosuppressive therapy within 6 months prior to first dose of MDX2003 (unless agreed otherwise between the medical monitor and the investigator on a case-by-case basis). NOTE: Non-systemic corticosteroids (eg, topical, inhaled) are allowed. The use of physiologic doses of corticosteroids may be approved after consultation with the medical monitor. Low-dose prednisolone for rheumatoid arthritis or similar conditions is allowed.
9. [10] Participant has received a live or live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1. (Sponsor discussion is required if participant needs live vaccine; vaccine administration follows institutional guidelines.)
10. [1] History of Grade 4 CRS or Grade 4 ICANS associated with any prior immune-effector therapy.
11. [11] Hepatitis B virus: Participants with positive hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) are excluded. Participants with positive hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) and negative HBsAg require negative hepatitis B polymerase chain reaction (PCR) before enrollment, and institutional guidelines for prophylaxis must be followed. Participants who are hepatitis B PCR positive will be excluded.
12. [12] Hepatitis C virus: Participants with positive hepatitis C antibody will need to have a negative hepatitis C ribonucleic acid (RNA) test before enrollment. Participants who are hepatitis C RNA positive will be excluded.
13. [13] Participant has known human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.
14. [14] Participant has a history of allogenic tissue or solid organ transplant, with the exception of corneal transplants. Participants with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) within 100 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 of MDX2003 are excluded.
15. [15] Participant is pregnant or breastfeeding.
16. [16] Participant has a known hypersensitivity to any components of MDX2003 or any of its excipients that, in the opinion of the investigator, suggests a high risk for a severe hypersensitivity reaction while on treatment.
17. [17] Participant has known hypersensitivity to allopurinol or rasburicase.
18. [18] Participant has a seizure disorder requiring therapy at the time of screening (such as steroids or anti-epileptics).
